title: Cost Escort: region-aware tier routing with eviction safebands
creator: Anya Patel
description: Implement a region-aware routing policy that balances cost (spot vs on-demand), GPU family selection, and tenant budget caps while protecting in-flight SLOs via an eviction-safeband mechanism. The feature should let us route requests into cheaper spot capacity aggressively when safe, gracefully degrade model variants (quantized/compact) when budgets are hit, and prefer lower-latency regions for SLO-sensitive tenants. It must integrate with the existing admission controller and the billing/usage service so we can enforce soft and hard caps per-tenant and per-project.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy available behind feature flag 'cost_escort_v1'
Cluster-level metrics emitted: routed_spot_pct, fallback_rate, safeband_violation_count
Per-tenant spend cap enforced as soft (throttle) and hard (reject) with configurable thresholds
Model-variant fallback chain defined and applied automatically when budget threshold crossed
System maintains 99th percentile request latency within configured SLO for prioritized tenants (within 10% of baseline) during normal load
End-to-end integration tests exercising spot eviction and automatic fallback to on-demand or compact model variants
design_notes: Introduce 'eviction safeband' concept: keep a buffer of on-demand capacity (percentage of tenant requests) allocated to tenants with high SLOs. When spot capacity is healthy, safeband stays low; on spot pressure we raise safeband and move more traffic to on-demand or compact variants.

Routing decision factors: tenant_priority, recent_spot_eviction_rate, tenant_spend_window (rolling 1h/24h), model_variant_latency_penalty, region_latency_delta. Each factor is scored and combined using a weighted linear policy; weights will be tunable via Console.

Budget enforcement: soft cap triggers auto-throttling + model-variant degradation; hard cap blocks non-essential routes. Soft cap uses a progressive response rather than immediate failover to avoid disrupting live sessions.

GPU selection: prefer accelerator families (A100 -> A10X -> T4) based on historical throughput per model architecture and per-tenant cost preference. Maintain per-region accelerator health signals to avoid routing to degraded SKUs.
Fallback model chain: full_fp32 -> int8_quant -> distilled_small -> prompt-cached-reply; each transition logs a regression event to quality-monitoring and can be annotated to the tenant in Console.

Interaction with scheduler: admission controller provides real-time hints (available_spot_capacity by region/family) and scheduler provides placement decisions. Routing returns placement hints rather than hard pins so scheduler can still respect host-level constraints.
Observability: emit detailed routing decisions (policy_score breakdown) for sampled requests to aid debugging and postmortems. Add dashboard for cumulative spend vs cap and fallback events by tenant.
Rollout plan: start with a small cohort of internal tenants, expand to opt-in customers, then global enable with conservative defaults. Feature flag allows per-tenant opt-out.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Initial RFC posted to internal docs -> Confluence draft linked. Design reviewed with runtime and billing teams. Action: add scheduler hint contract.
2026-02-20: Prototype scoring function implemented in staging (spot vs on-demand weight tunable). Early signal shows 18% cost reduction for non-SLO tenants without latency impact.

2026-02-28: Integration spike with billing completed; per-tenant rolling spend is now emitted to /metrics/billing/tenant_spend_window. Found performance delta in metric flush frequency — increased to 10s windows.

2026-03-06: Experiment: enabled safeband for two internal high-priority tenants. Observed safeband raised automatically on spot degradation; fallbacks triggered as expected. Logged fallback regressions to quality-monitoring.
2026-03-10: Security review pre-checks done (no new customer key material required). Pending automated tests covering edge cases (rapid fluctuation in spot capacity).
2026-03-13: Preparing canary rollout plan and writing e2e tests for eviction scenarios. Assigning QA to validate billing enforcement and user-visible annotations in Console.
decisions: Use soft caps with progressive throttling instead of immediate hard reroutes to reduce session disruption.
Expose policy weight knobs in Console but keep safeband tuning managed by runtime team initially.
Fallback model chain will be tenant-configurable per project; default chain will be enforced by runtime policy for safety.
Do not pin placements at routing layer; use placement hints to preserve scheduler autonomy and reduce placement churn.
Telemetry sampling set to 0.5% of requests for full policy_score payloads to control cardinality.
follow_ups: Add automated alerting for safeband_violation_count >= 5 in 1m for high-priority tenants
Run a 2-week canary with 10% of PROD traffic and compare cost/latency against control group
Add a Console page that visualizes tenant fallback chain events and gives suggested actions to reclaim budget
Post-launch: evaluate ML-based scoring (reinforcement) to replace linear policy if safeband oscillation persists
